references.text: Jesus' parallel exhortation in Matthew: 'Therefore you also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect' ([ref:Matt 24:44|Matthew 24:44]). This is the direct parallel to Luke 12:40 in Matthew's Gospel.

Jesus urges them to keep watch because they do not know on what day their Lord will come ([ref:Matt 24:42|Matthew 24:42]). The same theme of being prepared for the unexpected coming of the Son of Man.

The conclusion of the parable of the ten virgins: 'Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour' ([ref:Matt 25:13|Matthew 25:13]). Emphasizes the same motif of being ready because the time is unknown.

Jesus exhorts the disciples to pay attention and keep watch, for they do not know when the time will come ([ref:Mark 13:33-37|Mark 13:33-37]). The parable of the master who goes away on a journey, urging them to stay awake because they do not know when the master will return.

The immediate context where Jesus says the disciples should have their belts fastened and lamps burning, being like servants waiting for their master ([ref:Luk 12:35-36|Luke 12:35-36]). The basis for the exhortation to be ready in verse 40.

Jesus warns against being weighed down by drunkenness and the worries of life, so that day may come upon them unexpectedly, and urges them to keep watch and pray ([ref:Luk 21:34-36|Luke 21:34-36]). The same theme of the unexpected day and the need for vigilance.

Paul writes that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, but believers should not be caught off guard as if in darkness ([ref:1 Tess 5:2-4|1 Thessalonians 5:2-4]). The image of the thief in the night and the unexpected timing is directly linked to Jesus' words in Luke 12:39-40.
The day of the Lord will come like a thief ([ref:2 Pet 3:10|2 Peter 3:10]). Peter uses the same image that Jesus used to emphasize the unexpected nature of the Lord's coming.

Jesus says to the church in Sardis: 'If you do not keep watch, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you' ([ref:Åp 3:3|Revelation 3:3]). A direct parallel to Luke 12:40 with the image of the thief and the call to stay awake.

'Behold, I am coming like a thief! Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps their garments' ([ref:Åp 16:15|Revelation 16:15]). Contains both the thief motif and the blessing on those who are ready, closely connected to Jesus' words in Luke 12:40.

Daniel's vision of 'one like a son of man' coming with the clouds of heaven ([ref:Dan 7:13|Daniel 7:13]). The background for the expression 'the Son of Man is coming' that Jesus uses about himself in Luke 12:40.
